title: KB3g: the tight classes of the 18-point cover question for F2^7 - (7,1)/(8,2)/(6,0) PROVEN impossible, (11,7)/(9,9) gap pressed (outcome=partial, no new kappa)
body:
# KB3g: the tight classes of the 18-point cover question for F2^7 (outcome=partial, no new kappa)

Contributor: **Aaron Wang**, with help from opencode (substantial AI assistance in scoping, implementation, verification and writing; no model named; no independent human review claimed). No kappa, supplier, certificate or selected-frontier change.

## Change and mathematical scope

In the PR943 prefix-walk model ([PR 943](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/943) by Ross Richardson) a restored seven-source singleton word is universal exactly when its prefix set `P` covers: `P + P = F2^7`. This package executes the recorded remainder of [PR 2933](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2933) (its open questions 1 and 3) at the SET level, exact integers only: it decides the three tightest surviving classes of the 18-point cover question and presses the identity gap at (11,7)/(9,9). The question itself is **not** decided (no 18-point cover constructed, no split excluded outright), but its three tightest classes are gone.

Record chain, all authors verified against current ground truth with `gh pr view NNN --json author,title` at writing: [PR 2542](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2542), [PR 2634](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2634), [PR 2773](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2773), [PR 2870](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2870), [PR 2911](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2911), [PR 2933](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2933) by Aaron Wang (navinor); [PR 2691](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2691) by Nicholas Stone (NicholasStone) is the concurrent L=20 WORD census (recorded state only; untouched here).

## Verdict per class (exact integers throughout)

| Split | Class | PR 2933 status | Verdict here | Deciding evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| (10,8) | A-vanish (7,1), tight 32=32 | pinned to Sidon | PROVEN impossible | Fourier contradiction 175 vs 239; zero Sidon 5-pairs exist |
| (10,8) | D-vanish (8,2), tight 32=32 | pinned to Sidon | PROVEN impossible | all 28,815,360 equality configurations fail all three coverage lines |
| (12,6) | A-vanish (6,0), full odd half | pinned to full sumset | PROVEN impossible | no 6-set D of F2^5 has any 6-set X with X + D = F2^5 (all 169,911 normalized D walked) |
| (11,7) | no vanishing possible (L2) | row remainder 501 | narrowed: sum rho^2 >= 17 PROVEN | cross-sum multiplicity identity; no contradiction |
| (9,9) | no vanishing possible (L2) | row remainder 196 | narrowed: sum rho^2 >= 19 PROVEN | same identity; no contradiction |

Surviving after this package: (12,6) A-vanish (5,1)(4,2)(3,3) and D-vanish (9,3)(8,4)(7,5)(6,6); (10,8) A-vanish (6,2)(5,3)(4,4) and D-vanish (7,3)(6,4)(5,5); (11,7)/(9,9) at their row remainders with the new multiplicity conditions. Mirrors are identical by odd translation.

## (10,8) A-vanish (7,1): an exact Fourier contradiction, and empty enumeration

PR 2933's L7 pins every cover of the class to `|A0+A1| = 25` with `|A0| = |A1| = 5` (all 25 cross sums distinct) inside F2^5. With `f = 1_A0`, `g = 1_A1`, `h = 1_S` on `S = A0+A1`, Fourier over F2^5 gives `h_hat = f_hat * g_hat` pointwise, so Parseval forces `sum_{v != 0} h_hat^2 = 32*25 - 625 = 175` while `sum_{v != 0} f_hat^2 = sum_{v != 0} g_hat^2 = 32*5 - 25 = 135`. Both sizes are odd, so both Walsh transforms are odd and `f_hat^2 >= 1` pointwise; from `(f_hat^2 - 1)(g_hat^2 - 1) >= 0` one gets `sum h_hat^2 >= 135 + 135 - 31 = 239 > 175`: contradiction. The m=4 analogue computes `need = lower = 7` exactly (no contradiction), matching its 512 real covers - the identity is tight exactly where covers exist. Independently, the complete enumeration of normalized Sidon 5-pairs finds **zero** pairs (validated equal to full brute force, 5040 = 5040 at m=4; 2M random F2^5 pairs top out at `|A0+A1| = 23`), and coverage is independent of the free parameter `d1` (proven; machine-checked).

## (10,8) D-vanish (8,2): 28,815,360 equality configurations, all failing

L7 pins the class to `|A0+A1| = 16` and `|D0+D1| = 16`, disjoint with union the whole odd half. Normalizing `0` in `D0`, `0` in `D1` and `delta = 1` under GL(5,2) (half-translations preserve all four coverage lines - machine-checked), the A-side is parametrized by `w` (32 values, coverage independent of `w`, proven) and one choice element per `{x, x+1}` pair inside the complement of `D0+D1` (256 choices). Complete walk: 4,287,920 normalized Sidon 4-pairs, 112,560 with 1-invariant complement; all 28,815,360 (pair, choice) configurations fail **all three** translated coverage lines simultaneously (`fail_hist = {("I","II","III"): 28815360}`), zero covers. The reduction chain is validated end-to-end at m=4: the four L3 lines and a DIRECT `S + S = F2^5` cover test agree on all 4,096 analogue configurations, 512 covers accepted by both routes.

## (12,6) A-vanish (6,0): no full-sumset pair of 6-sets exists in F2^5

The class forces `A0+A1 = F2^5` (36 pairs, excess 4) and `A0 + D = A1 + D = F2^5` with `|D| = 6`. Two exact layers. First, a multiplicity classification (PROVEN): for any 6-set pair `X, Y` with `X + Y = F2^5`, `r = 1 + rho` with `sum rho = 4`, and per nonzero `v` the product `f_hat(v) * g_hat(v)` lies in `{0, 4, -4}`; exactly two excess patterns survive the Walsh constraints (`rho = 2+2` on two points, and `rho = 1+1+1+1` on an affine 2-flat `{p1, p2, p3, p1+p2+p3}`), while `4*delta_p`, `3+1` and `2+1+1` are PROVEN dead by exact integer constraints. Second, a complete transversal walk (PROVEN): `X + D = F2^5` says `X` hits all 32 translates of `D`; all 169,911 normalized 6-sets `D` were walked with a complete branch-on-uncovered search and **every** `D` has zero 6-set transversals, so lines (I'')/(II'') are unsatisfiable. Positive control: the same search recovers real transversals at m=3; a miniature cross-check finds no 3+3 full pair in F2^3 either (all 3,136 pairs).

## (11,7)/(9,9) identity gap: pressed, not cut

One bounded pivot on the named next identity (cross-sum multiplicities; the vanishing route is vacuous there by PR 2933's L2). With `A` an s-set and `D` a t-set covering `A + D = E = F2^6`, `r = 1 + rho` with `sum rho = s*t - 64`; both sides odd make both Walsh transforms odd, and the same pointwise inequality yields the exact necessary condition `64 * sum rho^2 - (s*t - 64)^2 >= (64*s - s^2) + (64*t - t^2) - 63`, i.e. `sum rho^2 >= 17` at (11,7) (excess 13) and `>= 19` at (9,9) (excess 17). Both bounds are attainable, so the identity does not contradict coverage: DEMOTED as an exclusion mechanism (the excess is too large for the rigidity that killed (7,1)). It does give PROVEN new necessary conditions: the all-ones excess pattern is impossible on both splits, and at (11,7) also the single-double pattern (2, 1^11). Validated positively on every odd-odd-split cover of F2^4. The row remainders 501/196 stand.

## Reproduce

Standard library only, CPython 3.12, from the repository root:

```sh
python3 -I -B research/f7-18point-tight-classes-seed4c1e7b30/test_engine.py
python3 -I -B research/f7-18point-tight-classes-seed4c1e7b30/verify.py quick
python3 -I -B research/f7-18point-tight-classes-seed4c1e7b30/verify.py novanish
python3 -I -B research/f7-18point-tight-classes-seed4c1e7b30/verify.py rows
python3 -I -B research/f7-18point-tight-classes-seed4c1e7b30/verify.py classes
python3 -I -B research/f7-18point-tight-classes-seed4c1e7b30/verify.py anchors
```

Expected markers: `Ran 13 tests ... OK`, `PASS_TIGHT_QUICK`, `PASS_TIGHT_NOVANISH`, `PASS_TIGHT_ROWS`, `PASS_TIGHT_CLASSES`, `PASS_TIGHT_ANCHORS`. The class walks are resumable with per-shard receipts (TIGHT-PROGRESS.json, one section per mode; TIGHT-C60-*.json per shard of the (6,0) walk; `run_tight.py merge60` merges them). Registered replay: `python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/f7-18point-tight-classes-seed4c1e7b30 --check-only` passes `PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS`.

## Scope and limitations

Set-level only inside PR943's abstract interface. Not checked: anything word-level (the repeated-state L=20 word census is Nicholas Stone's concurrent claim, [discussion 1166 comment 18954844](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18954844); untouched here), the 19-point cover question, walk-realizability of any cover, and any kappa, supplier, tariff or selected-frontier implication. The surviving non-tight classes are not decided and no claim is made about them. The (11,7)/(9,9) multiplicity conditions are necessary, not sufficient; no row of the PR 2911 remainder is excluded by them. The m=4 analogue controls validate the reduction chain but are not a proof at m=6; the m=6 results rest on the exhaustive enumerations (13 machine tests, byte-pinned engines) and the exact identities. The gap `20 <= f(7) <= 24` is unchanged. Discussion post: [FINDING/DONE comment 18975496](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18975496).

## Open next questions

1. **Decide the surviving non-tight classes** of (12,6) and (10,8): press L5's multi-vanishing grid (counts (x, y, y, x)) at two characters against the class floors, starting with (5,1) and (6,2). Why it matters: clearing both splits settles two of the four 18-point splits. Blocked by: nothing structural; a bounded joint enumeration.
2. **Find the sharper (11,7)/(9,9) identity**: combine the proven sum-rho^2 conditions with the even half `(A+A) u (D+D) = E` multiplicities (PR 2870 used only odd coverage) as a second layer on the 501/196 rows. Why it matters: those splits carry the other half of the question. Blocked by: no known coupling identity between odd-line cross-sum multiplicities and even-line self-sums.
3. **Search for an 18-point cover outside the decided classes**: seeded search over the (11,7)/(9,9) row remainder profiles with the new multiplicity conditions as admissibility filters. Why it matters: a construction keeps the L=22 route alive; search best remains 118/128 at k=18. Blocked by: nothing structural; a failed bounded search is not an exclusion.
